title: Non-invasive detection of vagal nerve response patterns in gastroparesis treatment
author: Matthew Ward
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bax7ifrn

steps.title: Review study and obtain consent
steps.instruction: Explain the study and informed consent document to the prospective subject, answer all questions, and obtain a signed consent before proceeding.

substeps.instruction: Review the nature of the study and the informed consent document with the subject.
Answer any questions the subject may have.
Obtain the subject’s signature on the informed consent document.

steps.title: Record GCSI survey and device settings
steps.instruction: Collect the subject’s symptom data and the current gastric electrical stimulation (GES) device parameters, then document them together.

substeps.instruction: Have the subject complete the Gastroparesis Cardinal Symptom Index (GCSI) survey.

Interrogate the GES device to determine current stimulus parameter settings, stimulating electrode impedance, and electrode configuration (bipolar or monopolar using the implanted pulse generator housing as return).
Record these parameters on a separate document that will be kept with the GCSI survey data.

steps.title: Prepare subject for cervical vagus recording
steps.instruction: Position the subject comfortably and clean the recording sites on the neck.

substeps.instruction: Instruct the subject to lie on their back with head and neck supported on pillows to avoid neck strain and reduce muscle‑artifact contamination.
Clean the skin over the left and right cervical vagus nerves with alcohol swabs and allow it to dry.

steps.title: Apply electrodes, gel, and record data
steps.instruction: Place cutaneous electrodes with conductive gel, record physiological signals with the GES device ON and OFF, and document electrode geometry.

substeps.instruction: Using the ADInstruments PowerLab System and cutaneous ECG electrodes, record Lead II ECG (for SKNA), the electrogastrogram, and electroneurograms (ENG) from the skin over the left and right mid‑cervical vagus nerves; apply a small amount of conductive electrolyte gel to each pad electrode before placement.
Record data with the GES device turned ON for at least 8 minutes without adjusting parameter settings.
Record data with the GES device turned OFF for at least 2 minutes.
Mark the ECG electrode locations and the common/ground electrode location on the provided figure.
Measure and record the straight‑line distance (cm) from the GES stimulating electrodes to the closest recording electrode on the left cervical vagus nerve.

Complete the checklist: record conduction distance (cm), confirm vagal electrode locations marked (YES/NO), confirm ≥8 min of data collected with GES ON (YES/NO), confirm ≥2 min of data collected with GES OFF (YES/NO).

steps.title: Remove electrodes, clean, and store data
steps.instruction: Safely detach electrodes, clean residual gel, and securely archive the recorded data.

substeps.instruction: Carefully remove the electrodes from the subject.
Gently wipe away any residual electrolyte gel with a clean cloth.
De‑identify the raw data and store it on a secure computer or server in accordance with IRB guidelines.
